caller_turns: My name is Leena. I am waiting under a bus shelter after work. The rain is loud enough that I almost missed the bus announcement.
The next bus is in forty minutes. I am not in danger, just damp and cross. What have I interrupted you doing?
I work at a small museum. Today we moved an enormous wooden cabinet three times before admitting it belonged where it started.
It was funny by the third move. Does anyone in your community have a talent for making extra work?
My lunch was cold noodles in a yellow tin. I forgot my fork and had to borrow one from the ticket office.
Do you usually eat with the others, or do people take their bowls away?
I like the sound of rain when I can stay indoors. Here it keeps bouncing off the roof onto my shoes.
What sound gets on your nerves up there?
A man at the far end of the shelter is trying to keep a paper bag dry. I offered him the spare bag from my pocket.
He said no at first, then changed his mind. We have not otherwise spoken.
Have you ever refused a perfectly useful thing just because someone offered it at the wrong moment?
I sometimes do that when I am tired. Tonight I would happily accept dry socks from almost anyone.
My bus has been delayed another ten minutes. Tell me one small thing that went wrong in your day.
I am not asking for a lesson about patience. Ordinary bad timing will do.
There is a break in the rain now. I can hear someone rolling the museum bins out behind the shelter.
I might put the phone in my pocket for a minute while I look for my ticket. Keep me company with something ordinary.

I am Tomas. I look after the little community radio studio on Thursdays. The microphone stand has developed a very theatrical squeak.
I have already checked the cable. This is the hinge complaining whenever anyone leans forward.
I put a note on the desk saying please stop leaning on this. Naturally I leaned on it while writing the note.
Are there repairs around your place that everyone has learned to work around?
We broadcast local notices and music. Tonight I am reading out the hours for a seed exchange.
The notices are handwritten. One of them looks as if it says bring your own goat, but I think it means coat.
Would you correct a mistake like that as you read, or stop and admit you could not make it out?
I once announced that the library would open at nine in the evening. Three people actually came.
They were amused about it. The librarian less so.
I am drinking water from a square green bottle. It makes a loud glug at exactly the wrong moment.
What do you keep within reach when you settle down to talk?
An older volunteer here insists on doing all the labels with a ruler. I used to think that was ridiculous, but his are the only ones still readable.
Did somebody older than you teach you a habit that seemed fussy at the time?
No grand wisdom required. I was thinking of labels and hinges.
The next presenter has arrived early, so I have a few minutes with nothing I need to do.
What would you do with a free ten minutes before supper?

I am Oren. I have six plant pots on the flat roof of my building. I went up to water them and found the wind had rearranged the empty pots.
The roof has a proper railing and a stair door. I am sitting safely by the door, feeling outnumbered by terracotta.
Three pots have beans. The others are marigolds, mint and one stubborn tomato plant.
Do you grow anything that is more trouble than it is worth?
My neighbour lent me a red watering can with a cracked handle. I keep forgetting to hold it underneath.
I ought to return it and buy one, but I have grown rather fond of its terrible handle.
Is there an object you keep using after it really ought to have been replaced?
The mint is thriving. Everything else seems to be negotiating with me.
I can smell somebody downstairs frying onions. That is making my gardening enthusiasm evaporate.
What would you eat if nobody else had a say in supper tonight?
Yesterday I promised a bean plant to my niece. She wanted to know how long before it was taller than she was.
I said I would ask the bean and get back to her. She thought that was a poor answer.
Were you patient with growing things when you were young?
I was impatient with almost everything at that age. I still dig up seeds sometimes to see if anything is happening.
The stair door keeps catching on a little stone. I have moved it twice and the wind has brought it back.
I am heading down shortly. Tell me about a small job you are putting off.

I am Sada. I mend costumes for a local theatre group. Tonight there are twelve identical black buttons on my table and one that only pretends to be identical.
I have put the odd button in a blue saucer so I stop sewing it onto things by mistake.
The coat belongs to a comedy. Its wearer has to fall through a door three times without losing the pockets.
Would you find that sort of repetition funny, or would once be enough?
I enjoy rehearsals more than opening nights. People are still willing to laugh at their own mistakes.
Do the people you live with laugh much when something goes wrong?
A young actor apologised to a chair after walking into it yesterday. The chair took it very well.
I am waiting for the iron to cool before I pack it away. That always takes longer than I expect.
Do you have an evening routine you start earlier than you really need to?
My scissors belonged to my aunt. They are heavy, and everyone who borrows them complains.
I think they are just used to lighter ones. They cut beautifully when you do not try to hurry.
What was the first tool you learned to use properly?
I keep a little notebook of repairs because I cannot rely on remembering which pocket tore last time.
I wrote coffee stain in it today, but that was the stain on the notebook itself.
The others have gone home. I can hear the cleaner moving chairs in the hall.
I have one button left to sew and then I am done. What remains of your evening?
